utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume our work. Good morning. Do the interpreters hear me? Good morning to them. That's fine. Does the Prosecution hear? Does the Defence hear? Very well. We're going to resume now for a day which may not be too long, but I would like things to be clear to everybody. Since the time which is not used today by the Prosecution will be counted as part of its time, whereas tomorrow, if not used, will not be counted because there have been changes at various levels which are regrettable but, in fact, it's the Tribunal that is responsible for that, and therefore it will not be counted against the Prosecution. Mr. Cayley I believe is going to conduct the examination. The floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, Counsel. The Prosecutor would now like to call a Major Oscar Meijboom, another Dutch army officer, an ECMM monitor from July of 1993 until January of 1994. He served predominantly in the municipalities of Kiseljak, Fojnica, Kresevo, and Visoko. He will speak in his testimony of a front-line visit that he made to the 3rd battalion of the Ban Jelacic brigade of the HVO. This took place in an area known as Otigosce in the municipality of Kiseljak. He will state that at this front-line position, he witnessed Bosnian Muslim men digging military fortifications for the HVO, and he will speak of the conversations that he had with the battalion commander at that location, a Mr. Branko Stanic, and he will tell the court about that man's views on Muslims in Kiseljak and of atrocities committed against the Muslim people in Kiseljak. Based on what he was told by the HVO in Kiseljak, he will explain to you the HVO command structure in that area as he saw it throughout his tour. He will speak briefly of his visits to the Rotilj village, which over seven months he visited 15 to 20 times. He will speak of conditions there, of the evidence that he saw of looting of this village and of the physical abuse of Muslim detainees. He will speak of Serb involvement in the municipality of Kiseljak to the HVO, of the military assistance provided to the HVO in the form of T-55 main battle tanks which he himself witnessed in the municipality of Kiseljak. He will tell the Court of his conversations with the HVO authorities on the assistance that the Serbs were providing in moving supplies into Kiseljak municipality. He will tell the Court how, in October of 1993, he sought population statistics from the HVO authorities in Kiseljak and Kresevo indicating the ethnic composition of those municipalities prior to the war. He will then give the figures as he knew them of the number of Muslims living in Kiseljak and Kresevo by October of 1993. Next he will speak of his attempts in October of 1993 to enter the village of Stupni Do in the municipality of Vares, and how the HVO refused to allow entry into that village because of supposed combat operations, how he saw truckloads of HVO troops leaving that village and how those troops explained that they were involved in work they did not like doing. He will speak of conversations that he had with the brigade commander, the HVO brigade commander, Emil Harah in Vares, and later with a conversation with Ivica Rajic at the HVO headquarters in Vares. Lastly, he will speak of a time in November when the International Community blamed Ivica Rajic for what had occurred in Stupni Do and for a number of other incidents involving NGOs and how he perceived that although Ivica Rajic was supposedly removed by the HVO authorities from command in Kiseljak, in reality, the man was not removed at all but remained in a position of command in Kiseljak, and the witness will broadly speak of what he perceived happening in Kiseljak at the time. His testimony is relevant to paragraphs 4, 5.2, Count 1; persecution, Counts 5 to 10; wilful killing and causing serious injury, Counts 11 to 13; destruction and plunder of property, Counts 15, 16, 17, and 18; inhumane treatment and taking of hostages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you for the summary. Mr. Dubuisson, would you have the witness brought in, please? There is no Dutch interpreter today?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: The witness is testifying in English, Mr. President. I spoke to the Dutch Ministry of Defence last night. They were reluctant, but they've agreed, and the witness has also agreed to testify in English. (The witness entered)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That will speed things up. Do you hear me, Major. Presiding Judge speaking to you. Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First of all, good morning. Tell us your family name, your given names, and your rank. Remain standing, please, until you have read your oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Meijboom, first name Oscar, I'm a Major in the Dutch army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you spell your name for us, please? Please spell your name. Before you read the oath, would you please spell your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: M-E-I-J-B-O-O-M.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: How do you pronounce it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Meijboom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, Major Meijboom, would you please read the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I promise to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. You have come at the request of the Prosecution as part of the trial of General Blaskic, the accused in this courtroom. You are going to answer the questions asked by the Prosecutor, you will speak freely. According to a procedure, which I'm sure Mr. Cayley has explained to you. When the Prosecution asks you a question, you can look at the person asking the question, but when you answer, please answer directly facing the Judges. Thank you. Mr. Cayley, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Cayley

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Meijboom, when I ask you a question, if you could pause slightly before you answer my question because I am being interpreted as you are, simultaneously, so it assists the interpreters. You joined the Dutch army in 1980?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You attended the officer training school in Breda in the Netherlands which was two years; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you then went into the medical branch of the Dutch army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've held a number of platoon and company commands over both medical and administrative personnel in the Dutch army?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've also held a number of staff positions in the Dutch army?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you're presently the second in command of the Dutch army garrison at Zoutkamp in Groningen?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're a Major now?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've done two tours of duty with the European Community Monitoring Mission?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One from July of 1993 to January 1994 in Central Bosnia, and one from January 1995 to August 1995 in Bihac?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were in Central Bosnia, you were in a team that was mainly responsible for the municipalities of Kiseljak, Fojnica, Kresevo, and Visoko; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, concentrating on that period of time, from July of 1993 to January of 1994, I want you to recall some visits that you made to front-line positions in Kresevo and Tarcin, and Otigosce and Fojnica, and specifically a visit that you made in September of 1993 to the Otigosce/Fojnica front-line. Could you explain what occurred on that visit to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I visited the frontlines several times. I passed them two or three times a week. When I visited the front-line, I visited together with the battalion commander in the area, it was Mr. Branko Stanic. He wanted to show us the frontlines, and we came at the front-line and we saw his soldiers guarding some people working at the trenches. We asked Mr. Stanic about these people because they were unprotected, they didn't wear arms, as the other soldiers, so we asked him about these guys, and he just laughed and said these were some of his men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this an HVO position?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was on the front-line from the battalion facing the other troops in Fojnica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Branko Stanic, who was he?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: He was the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of this HO battalion?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of these men were there digging military fortifications?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Five or six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen any of them before?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I had seen two of these men before in a village named Rotilj near Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and the other monitors come to a conclusion about who these people were digging these trenches?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, we did. These people were Muslim people from the village of Rotilj, they were men in the age of 40 to 60, and they were kept in Rotilj and they were used to work on the trenches in Otigosce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of physical condition were these people in?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Not really bad but not good as well. They were poorly dressed and they were a bit skinny.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to Mr. Stanic about his views on the Muslim population in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, we did. In fact, Mr. Stanic always gave his view on the Muslim population always when we met him. He had a very extreme view. He stated that he would like to kill them all if they would take some tearing (unclear), he wouldn't make prisoners, he would kill them or nail them on a cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he speak about these matters in front of his men?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever see the men of this HVO battalion based at Otigosce actually committing any war crimes?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We saw them once, it was near Fojnica, they were burning houses and looting houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away from them were you when you saw this taking place?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: How far away from ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away from these soldiers that you observed looting, what was the distance?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We were close to them and we even spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown the first exhibit, which is a map? What exhibit number is this, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 430.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before coming into the courtroom today, I asked you to mark on a map the position, as best as you could recall it, of the HVO front-line at Otigosce. Is that the line that you marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is part -- this one (indicated). It's part of the front-line of the HVO battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're pointing at the orange sort of squiggle within the blue square?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you visit that front-line; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, we visited twice but we passed it several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if the witness could be shown the next exhibit, which is 431?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Major Meijboom, prior to you testifying here today, I asked you to draw out for me the command structure as you understood it in Kiseljak. Is this the diagram that you drew for me?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, you have at the bottom left-hand corner the Otigosce battalion, the 3rd battalion. How do you know that Branko Stanic was the commanding officer of that battalion?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: First of all, because he introduced himself like that, he was addressed as a commander by his men, and also from HVO barracks in Kiseljak, we were told that this battalion was stationed out in Otigosce and that we could meet the battalion commander, Mr. Stanic, over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, how do you know that Mr. Iv Kluges was the battalion commander in Cresol, the 2nd battalion?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It's the same story. We met Mr. Kulis, he introduced him like that, he was addressed like a commander, also by HVO barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could explain how you knew that Mr. Ivica Rajic occupied the three positions that you've indicated on that diagram, certainly during your period of service in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We had the first meeting with Mr. Rajic and then he introduced himself as the commander of operational group, the brigade in Kiseljak, and the 1st battalion in Kiseljak, and he was also addressed by all international organisations, including UNPROFOR, as the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that Mr. Blaskic was the operational zone commander over arching all of these other units?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We know because Mr. Rajic said so. We heard several times from liaison officer Vinko Lucic, he spoke about Mr. Blaskic as the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me a little bit more about Mr. Vinko Lucic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Vinko Lucic was the liaison officer from HVO barracks in Kiseljak to all international organisations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How regularly did you deal with him?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Three to four times a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to whom did he report?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: To Mr. Rajic, his commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, finally on that diagram you have the Bobovac brigade under the command of Emil Harah. How do you know that that unit fell under the command of Ivica Rajic?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Because he told this to us and we met -- in fact, Vares was not my area, but we met Mr. Harah a couple of times and he also addressed Mr. Rajic as being his commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Exhibit 85, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: This is Mr. Lucic, Vinko Lucic, the liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if the witness could be shown Exhibit 339?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic (indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there ever an occasion when you were with Vinko Lucic and you wished to see Mr. Rajic and it wasn't possible to see him?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, there were several occasions that we couldn't talk to him. One of the occasions, he said Mr. Rajic is not available because he is on the radio with his commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we can move on to Rotilj, and I know you visited on a large number of occasions, and I don't wish you to speak about every visit, but if you could summarise to the court your visits over a seven-month period and end, I think, with one of the visits which was most memorable towards the end of November of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, as you said, we visited the village several times, and during these visits, starting in July, we saw that the population -- or the village got overcrowded. Originally there were 200 and in the end there were about 800 inhabitants. When we were there, this particular situation, some women came to us and they claimed to be raped. They showed us bruises on their body to prove this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition of the people in Rotilj by November of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: They were in need of all kinds of things. In fact, there was no organisation that could take -- could care for them, they needed food, medicines, medical treatment, stoves, blankets. In fact, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people free to leave the village of Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, they were not. They were kept there. The area was sealed by HVO and civil police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the HVO ever tell you why these people were kept in the village of Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: The liaison officer of HVO, Mr. Lucic, and the mayor of Kiseljak, Mr. Boro, Josip Boro, told us that these people were kept there, in fact, for two reasons. First reason, for their own safety, and second reason, to keep there as some kind of a stock for future exchanges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all of the people in this village of Rotilj Bosnian Muslims, these 800 people?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any evidence of looting of houses and beating of the detainees in Rotilj village?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We didn't see it happen, but we saw the results. We saw houses burned and furniture thrown out and taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have a discussion with Vinko Lucic about a particular incident of looting and raping that happened towards the end of November of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, we had. We heard -- I don't recall from whom -- that something happened in Rotilj, and when we asked Lucic about it, he said that the matter was under investigation. It was about one man being killed, one man wounded, and probably women raped, and it was done by three or four uniformed men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the results of any investigation into this matter?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you describe the people in Rotilj as very frightened when you visited them?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Mostly because they weren't sure of their lives, they felt like they were being held in prison and they weren't sure what the future would bring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see able-bodied men being taken from Rotilj village while you were there by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, we saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could now move on to the next part of your testimony which concerns the involvement of the Bosnian Serb army in Kiseljak, and if you can summarise to the Judges your observations in that respect?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We heard from people in Canadian battalion that they saw some tanks T-55s, 15 to 25 of these things in the area of Gromiljak, it's close to Kiseljak, and when we went to see ourselves, we saw five or six of these tanks, T-55.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these HVO tanks?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, they were not HVO tanks because HVO didn't have tanks at that moment in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to whom did these tanks belong?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know to whom they belonged at that moment, but they came from Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were these tanks actually doing in the area?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: They were there to support an offensive in the direction of Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was running the offensive in the direction of Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: A brigade in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An HVO brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: HVO brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the mayor of Kiseljak tell you about supplies coming into the municipality of Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We asked him about the supplies because Kiseljak was said to be a pocket and we always saw the shops full of all kinds of fresh things, so we asked them how they get the goods in, and he explained that it came in with convoys coming from Croatia where the goods were bought with money from a bank account which was sponsored by foreign Croats, so they could bring in a convoy if they paid the Serbs enough money to let them through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I think in October of 1993, you sought certain details of the ethnic composition of Kiseljak and Kresevo before the war, and I'd be grateful if you could tell the Court about that investigation in which you were involved?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We were interested in ethnic population before war, and so we went to the town halls in Kiseljak and in Kresevo, and there we got the figures, and we were mainly interested in the Croat and the Muslim population. In Kiseljak, they told us in the town hall that before war the total number of inhabitants was around 24.000 of which almost 10.000 Muslim. In Kresevo, we did the same, we went to the town hall and there they told us that before war, there were around 7.000 inhabitants of which 1500 were Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In October of 1993, did you investigate how many Muslims were left in Kiseljak and Kresevo?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In Kresevo, there were approximately 150 kept in a school building, and in Kiseljak area, there were around 800 kept in Rotilj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So a large number of Muslims were no longer living in Kiseljak and Kresevo?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned earlier that there were 800 Muslim people kept in the village in Rotilj. Did you visit other villages in the Kiseljak area to find the possible presence of Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I visited I think almost all the villages in the area. During my visits, all the villages, except for Palez, were free of Muslim population. In Palez there was some left maybe 20, but during my period, they also moved, whether to Rotilj or somewhere else, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if we can move to the attack on the village of Stupni Do, and I know that you were involved from an early stage and then you went on leave back to the Netherlands, but if you could explain to the Judges the events of the 23rd, 24th, and 25th of October of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes. Early in the morning of 23rd, we were sent to Vares area to investigate on the matter that should have happened in Stupni Do. We didn't know at that moment what happened, but we heard rumours that something happened in Stupni Do, and the head of the coordination centre didn't think it was safe enough for one team to go in, so he sent us with V-4 team. We went there, and we were first stopped by an Armija checkpoint and they told us it wasn't safe to go in the area because of fighting that were going on. At this checkpoint, we heard that there was fighting going on because of small arms fire and heavy machine-gun fire. The other team leader, Mr. Rolf Weckesser, an officer in German army, didn't want to go in because he felt it wasn't safe enough so we went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think on the 24th of October, you actually decided to return to Vares. Can you tell the Judges about that?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes. The next day we tried again. That's the day we passed the checkpoint of the Armija, then we entered the HVO checkpoint near the road to Stupni Do. There we were stopped again and we were not allowed to go in the direction of Stupni Do because we needed the permission of the brigade commander. While we were there, we saw three trucks with soldiers coming back from the direction of Stupni Do, and Mr. Weckesser, the other team leader, spoke with the help of his interpreter with the soldiers, and these soldiers told him that they had to do a job they didn't like, and that they had nothing to do with what happened to the people in Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say you were stopped on the road to Stupni Do. By whom were you stopped?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: By HVO checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which brigade commander were they referring you to?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: The brigade commander from Vares, Emil Harah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when Colonel Weckesser had this conversation with these HVO soldiers, the monitors, I assume, discussed this amongst themselves. What did you interpret this to mean, what they had stated to you?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, because of the fact that the soldiers came back from the direction of Stupni Do and we saw smoke coming from the direction of Stupni Do and the things they said, we assumed that they had to do some kind of a cleaning job, so getting rid of dead bodies and burning things down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go and see Emil Harah?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We were told by him that we couldn't enter because of the fact that there was still fighting going on in the area, so we went back again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you returned to Zenica on that day?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 25th of October, you came back again to Vares; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct. That day we were together with Mr. William Stutt, a Canadian officer, he was the head of the coordination centre, and we went to Vares to the sport hotel where the headquarters of the brigade was to meet Mr. Harah to get permission to go to Stupni Do, but when we came there it wasn't Mr. Harah who was in command, it was Mr. Rajic who welcomed us and introduced a new man which we didn't know before, it was Mr. Bozic, Kresimir Bozic, and he told us that was the new commander, but this new commander didn't do any talking. Mr. Rajic told us that we couldn't go to Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever get into Stupni Do yourself?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you then went on leave, did you not, back to the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I right in saying that you returned to Kiseljak in the middle of November?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you came back from leave, did you discover that the command of the HVO in Kiseljak had apparently changed?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes. We were told by Mr. Lucic that Ivica Rajic was no longer in command and that the commander was now Mario Bradara, it was his former second in command, and Mr. Rajic would act as an advisor for the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why had Mr. Rajic apparently been removed from command of the HVO in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, there were two reasons. One reason was the affair in Stupni Do, what happened there, because Rajic was blamed by International Organisations and, in fact, by everybody about what happened to Stupni Do, and the other reason was Mr. Rajic's attitude toward the International Organisations and the fact that he threatened a UNHCR field officer in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stupni Do was a Muslim village, was it not?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, had Mr. Rajic, in fact, been removed from his command position in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, not effectively because he was still there and he acted as an advisor to his former second in command, so you could say he was still in command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody in ECMM take this removal seriously of Mr. Rajic?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, nobody did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could apply for admission into evidence, Mr. President, of Exhibits 430, 431? I have no further questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. It's 10.45. We can begin with the cross-examination. Mr. Hayman? You are now going to be asked some questions by Defence counsel. Cross-examined by Mr. Hayman

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, good morning, Major.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First with respect to your observations at Otigosce beginning in or about September of 1993. You said that Branko Stanic was the HVO commander there?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What unit or brigade was this? Was this the -- it's labelled on Exhibit 431 as the Otigosce battalion. Had it always been based in Otigosce?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know where it had been based, but in my period, it was based in Otigosce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, hadn't it been the HVO unit in Fojnica prior to establishing a command in Otigosce?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you author a background report prepared within the ECMM organisation on or about the 6th of October, 1993, dealing with the subject of Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We did prepare a background report, yes, together with the other team members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that report reflect and is it true that in Fojnica, the fighting began on the 3rd of July, 1993, by a Muslim first action?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know whether that is true because that's information I didn't confirm myself because I wasn't there at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, we'll show the witness a copy of his report, and perhaps it will refresh his recollection. This report, Mr. President, exists only in English at this time. Our apologies. It is four pages in length.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can make an observation? This is a witness that was in Bosnia for nearly seven months, and I have attempted to complete an examination-in-chief in 30 minutes. Mr. Hayman is now moving almost immediately into areas that were simply not covered in my examination-in-chief. Moreover, he's showing the witness a report to refresh his memory when the witness has already stated that he cannot confirm this information because he wasn't there at this time. It's a pointless exercise that we're going through and it's outside the scope of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, when a witness tenders an exhibit identifying a unit in a particular place and he wrote a report concerning where that unit actually came from, that unit was attacked by the BH army, driven out of Fojnica, together with some five to ten or more thousand Croat refugees. He doesn't remember; that's fine. I accept that. But he should be able -- he should be allowed, I should be permitted, to show him his prior report so that the Court can have accurate information with respect to this unit and this man, Branko Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now Mr. Hayman is giving evidence before the court, I see, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, it seems possible to me that the Defence might want to try to respond within this cross-examination about the command structure, but I would point out to you, don't regret having been able to be -- able to synthesise things so well. You of course have your right in the redirect as well if you consider that it would be better to go back and ask further questions. But for the time being, we're going to ask Mr. Hayman to continue using this document as part of his cross-examination, and I will be very attentive to make sure that we do not go beyond what is permitted within the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D453.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That must be an error, Mr. President. It was translated as D453, but we don't have that many Defence exhibits yet. Perhaps the registrar could restate the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That was a mistake. It's 153. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dubuisson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But remain within the scope of the command structure, Mr. Hayman. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will stay within the scope of the direct examination, with respect to this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, at the end of the report, do you see your initials?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You certified that this document was accurate and authentic at the time that you first tendered it to the Office of the Prosecutor; correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does this refresh your recollection that the fighting began in Fojnica on the 3rd of July, 1993, by a Muslim first action against the HVO unit that was then resident in Fojnica and was then commanded by Branko Stanic?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, it is, as I told you, I didn't witness it myself. As all the information before my period, this is a background report, it gives some history of the area. Because it's history I didn't see or confirm it myself, this is information, whether from authorities or from former teams. That's all I can say about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your colleagues in the ECMM believe it to be true and that's why they put it in this report?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has just stated that is all he can say about this report. He's made his answer quite clear, and I would ask that Mr. Hayman move on to another area of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It's curious, Mr. President. The witness has never disavowed ECMM reports on direct examination by the Prosecutor. I make that observation. I will continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told where Branko Stanic had come from when he first came to the HVO unit in Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: You mean where he came --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Hayman, but be brief.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: You mean where he came from originally or ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told what his prior occupation had been before coming to the HVO unit in Fojnica, I believe in approximately January of 1993, or coming to Fojnica in approximately January of 1993? Were you told that he had been selling insurance in Vienna for the prior seven years, Major? Is that what you had been told?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I had been told by Branko Stanic himself that he was a sales -- seller in Austria. I don't know how he came to Fojnica or anywhere else, but I know he told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He told you that had been his prior occupation; correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say, Major, that your understanding is, again referring to the chart which is Exhibit 431, that this Otigosce battalion of the HVO is a unit that left Fojnica after an attack on it by the BH army and then resettled or relocated in Otigosce; is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, it's not my understanding because it happened before I was there and there was constant fighting going on in the area between Otigosce and Fojnica and the troops were moving back and forward, so that's all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an HVO unit in Fojnica at the time you arrived in the theatre in the middle of July 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you described some burning or looting of houses near Fojnica on one occasion that you witnessed. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It was -- I think it was around October '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say outside Fojnica --

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It was in the direction of Bacovici, it was close to Bacovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it near the front-line at the time?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, there were some fighting, fighting going on, and an HVO battalion took some terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how these houses were ignited? Were they ignited during fighting, during the take-over of the terrain? Were they ignited after the fighting? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It happened while the fighting was still going on, some of the soldiers were fighting and other soldiers were looting and destroying houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing? Destroying houses is a conclusion. Can you describe what you saw?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I can. They set fire on the houses and they throw out furniture and things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the front-line at the time?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Maybe -- well, there was no steady front-line at that time because there was fighting going on, so the old front-line from HVO was about one kilometre, one and a half kilometre from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many houses did you see being destroyed or damaged?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Four, five, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report that information within the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't remember that. Maybe I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to give us a more specific date?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, returning to Exhibit 431. Is it your testimony that this -- well, strike that. During what period of time is it your testimony that Exhibit 431 depicts the organisational scheme of the relevant portion of the HVO set forth in this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: The organisation, during my whole time, only the command structure in the Bobovac brigade changed, as I told you, before. And I told you also about the fact that Rajic was -- moved from his command and being put as an advisor of his former second in command, but the organisation of the battalions and the brigade stayed the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the first of those changes occurred on or about October 25th, 1993, is that right, with respect to the removal of Mr. Harah?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after that point in time, we would have to start modifying this chart in order for it to accurately reflect the persons who held the positions reflected in it; correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Kiseljak pocket or enclave, did they have access to Herzegovina and Mostar through Serb territory? Could that be arranged and was that possible?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Kiseljak enclave or pocket, did they have access to the Vitez pocket?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: All kinds of ways. You mean physical access?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How could those in the Kiseljak pocket travel to the Vitez pocket other than under escort by UNPROFOR or ECMM?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Just by using a mountain road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about this road.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: As we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about this road. Where is this road located?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It's located in the mountains -- well, there are several of these roads in the mountains between Vitez and Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do they transit BH army territory?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was no problem for you to use them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Remain within the scope of the direct examination, please, Mr. Hayman. Complete your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, an organisational chart like this, to have meaning, presumes that orders are followed; correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If orders are not followed, then it's not very meaningful; correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you. There was an incident involving the destruction or blowing up of the road from Visoko to Kiseljak; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is outside the scope of the examination-in-chief, completely outside --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We have left the examination-in-chief completely now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: They have given you a chart and this witness will testify that orders from the top box to the second box were not followed. That's directly responsive and relevant to the impression, the testimony, that this witness is trying to give the Court, and we must be allowed to present that testimony to the Court, and I proffer -- he will testify he was told by the HVO in Kiseljak that Ivica Rajic refused to follow and would not follow direct orders from Colonel Blaskic, and I ask to be permitted to present that testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: After having consulted my colleagues, Mr. Cayley, you decided to have the witness speak about the command structure, and Mr. Hayman is using his arms to continue this discussion. So Mr. Hayman, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will attempt to be brief on this line of inquiry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, on or about the 9th of October, 1993, did you report that the road from Visoko to Kiseljak had been made impassable by a large crater as a result of a detonation, and that Ivica Rajic had stated to the U.N. BH headquarters that he did not want the road repaired?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you subsequently told, on the 11th of October, 1993, by Vinko Lucic that Blaskic had given a direct order to Rajic to repair the road but that Rajic had replied that the road would stay closed until the evacuation of wounded from Novi Bila was realised, despite Blaskic's order to repair it and not to link the repair to the evacuation of the wounded? Were you also told that, sir?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I was told that by Vinko Lucic, but, in fact, the road was repaired, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long later -- how much time later was the road repaired after you were told Blaskic had given a direct order on or about the 11th of October, 1993, to Ivica Rajic to repair the road and Mr. Rajic had responded he would not? How much later was the road repaired?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many days later, but I would guess, I would say three or four days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps during the break you can review your reports and see if, in fact, you first reported that the road was reopened some ten days after the 11th of October, and I can assist you during the break in reviewing those reports, if you would be so kind. You were shown Exhibit 85, a photograph which includes, among others, Vinko Lucic. Perhaps you should be shown the photo so you have it in mind. Do you know when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were shown another photograph, Exhibit 339, which included a depiction of Ivica Rajic on a podium of some sort. Do you have that photo in mind?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Ivica Rajic received orders directly from General Petkovic in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Not as I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether General Petkovic visited the Kiseljak enclave and met directly with Ivica Rajic during your tour of duty in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I heard so, but I didn't witness it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a military man, do you think it's more likely if Rajic and Petkovic were in the Kiseljak enclave together and Blaskic was in the Vitez enclave which, according to you, was accessible only by a mountain road which went through BH army territory, is it likely that Petkovic would give orders --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can I finish my question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. This is pure speculation. Mr. Hayman wanders beyond the scope of the examination-in-chief and, two, he's asking the witness to give opinion about facts of which he is not aware. We are now entering the realm of speculation, and the witness should not be required to answer questions such as these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Don't ask for speculation, so don't speculate, Mr. Hayman. Ask your questions directly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I wasn't able to finish my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer it without speculating?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But it was very long. You're right, Mr. Hayman, ask shorter questions. Go more directly to where you want to go. Otherwise, the Prosecution is going to say that you're speculating when you start with such long introductions. It's difficult to know where you're going. Ask your questions directly, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's turn to the subject of Rotilj village. During your visits to the village of Rotilj, were you told that a medical doctor visited the village on a weekly basis?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told, during your visits to Rotilj village, that foodstuffs and supplies, soap and other similar personal items, were delivered to the village on a regular basis by Caritas in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: There were some goods delivered in Rotilj, and not by Caritas, it was delivered by a Muslim organisation, and it wasn't sufficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony is the only food aid delivered to Rotilj between July 1993 and January 1994 was delivered by Merhamet, a Muslim aid organisation; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that was the only aid they got because I didn't know that, I only know what they told me. They told me they had some aid from Merhamet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, do you still have many questions, in order to try to organise our schedule today? Perhaps you would prefer that we would take our break right away? Then there would be the redirect possibility from Mr. Cayley and any questions that the Judges might want to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I do have additional questions. It's not lengthy, but perhaps 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We're going to take a break for 20 minutes

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume the hearing. Have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, during the break, did you have a chance to review your reports and see when you first reported that the Kiseljak-Visoko road was repaired?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first report that it had been repaired?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I think it's in my report. It was the 12th, 11th or 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that report says?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know this report by heart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your testimony is, on the 12th of November, you reported that the road was repaired, had been repaired? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I can make this testimony if I have my report here so I can read exactly what date because I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You looked at it during the break. I didn't show you a copy. Could you be shown what you refreshed your memory with during the break, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: The witness actually looked at his statement because we couldn't locate the report, so if Mr. Hayman uses the statement that he made to the Office of the Prosecutor ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you using the statement or are you using the report, Mr. Hayman? We're not going to spend too much time with the report for the time being. Which document are you using? Which document did the witness take a look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: He says he looked at his statement. Mr. Cayley has indicated he looked at his statement. The report and the statement say the same thing, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read to you a section of your statement, Major, and ask you if this is what you're referring to. Page 4 of your statement to the Office of the Tribunal Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go slowly, Mr. Hayman, please, for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "On 12 October, 1993, I had another meeting with Vinko Lucic. He told me that Ivica Rajic stated that the Visoko-Kiseljak road would stay closed until the evacuation of the wounded of the Novi Bila hospital was realised, although Colonel Blaskic gave a direct order to Ivica Rajic to repair and open the road immediately and not to connect it with the evacuation of the Novi Bila hospital." Are you referring to that statement?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I'm not referring to any statement. I'm just listening to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You said you referred to your statement and your statement indicated that by the 11th or 12th of October, 1993, the road was open. I'm reading you a portion of your statement which indicates that, on the 12th of October, you were told that Ivica Rajic had said, in substance, "The road is not being opened, and I don't care that Colonel Blaskic gave me an order to open it," and not to link it with any other issue. Those two are inconsistent. So I'm asking you, is there some other portion of your testimony upon which you rely with respect to your testimony that the road was open by the 11th or 12th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let's not make the questions too complicated, Mr. Hayman. Things are becoming very complicated. You read part of the statement to the witness and asked him whether he confirms that. That's a clear question. Your last sentence is really very ambiguous; it's got several connotations. Let me turn to the Major. You have just been quoted a passage from your statement. Do you confirm it, "Yes" or "No"? That's all.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Sorry, but I got your -- I didn't get your translation, but I understood what you were asking me in French. Part of the declaration that he read, about what Mr. Vinko Lucic told me, is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I found the next relevant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the next page, page 5, you state in your statement that on the 20th of October, which is eight days after the 12th and nine days after the 11th, when you first learned that Blaskic had ordered Rajic to reopen the road, on the 20th of October, "I saw that the road was repaired." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen that the road was repaired prior to the 20th of October when you reported it?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no Croatian translation. It's a big problem for our client, from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The microphones are coming on by themselves, which may be related to the problem. Our microphones, since the break, have been coming on and off spontaneously. Mine off, and my colleague and my client's on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Oh, all right. Well, if we have got to start everything all over again, that's going to be complicated. You should have said something earlier. You should have told us earlier. I think that we're going to take a five-minute break in order to fix the problem. Very well. It will be better to do that then. All right. We're going to suspend the hearing for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't know why I keep finding myself on another channel here. Registrar, do you guarantee to us now that everything is going to operate perfectly?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, I cannot guarantee that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, maybe we'll have some luck. All right. Things seem to be fixed. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I don't think it's necessary to repeat any of the final dialogue. We will ensure that it's translated appropriately for our client, and he waives any right to have it repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. All right, General Blaskic, do you agree with that? Is that all right, General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: His microphone is not working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, Mr. Blaskic says "I agree," but I can't say that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've understood the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is a perfect example of a conference between client and counsel. All right. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Returning for a moment to Exhibit 431, Major, which we would like to see if we can have it provided to you. My question to you is: In the Dutch army, would you have the same commander at three different levels of command in the way that Ivica Rajic here occupies positions at three different levels of command? Would that happen on a permanent basis in the Dutch army, if you know?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On a permanent basis?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, it is possible. I don't know whether it happens at the moment right now, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When would that be done in the Dutch army?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Normally when there is a lack of officers from a certain category or of a certain knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's return to Rotilj, the village. During your leave of absence on approximately the 31st of October, 1993, did ECMM officers report that Caritas was making regular deliveries of aid to the village of Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It's correct that I was on leave at that time, and my team member did report that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the same aid, on a per-capita basis, was given to the inhabitants of Rotilj as was given to other Croat inhabitants of the Kiseljak municipality by Caritas?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know myself whether there was aid given by Caritas to the people in Rotilj because it's something someone else reported.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know anything about the quantity or parity and distribution; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the summer and fall of 1993, were there approximately 15.000 refugees in the Kiseljak municipality?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: At most. I think it is somewhere around 12.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those displaced persons include armed persons, including soldiers of the HVO, who had previously been in Travnik, Kakanj, and Vares?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It was just the whole population in Kiseljak, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including armed populations or soldiers from those three other locations; correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Which other locations are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Travnik, Kakanj, and Vares.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know whether they had been there before, but it's just the population that was in the Kiseljak pocket at that time, and there were people from all over, from everywhere, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that include soldiers that had withdrawn or retreated from other locations, Croat soldiers?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It included the soldiers who were in Kiseljak pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Can you tell the court, were the Muslim inhabitants of Rotilj, in your judgement, were they safer inside the village of Rotilj than they would have been if they had been living outside the village in some other location in the Kiseljak municipality?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: They weren't safe in any place, so I don't think you can speak of safe or less safe. People died in Rotilj, people were killed in Rotilj, so they weren't safe anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not able to make a comparison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said the Muslim inhabitants were not free to leave Rotilj. How is it they were kept captive in Rotilj? By what means? Patrols? Fences? How were they kept captive in this village?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: The roads were closed by civilian police and military checkpoints. They were patrolled, and there was a regular visit of military and civil police and also normal military people in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many checkpoints were there?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: On the road from Kiseljak to Rotilj, one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other checkpoints around the village, that is, on any roads -- roads and tracks running in and out of the village? On the other sides of the village, were there any other checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It wasn't able to enter the village from the other side by car, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that no one could walk out of the village because there were constant HVO patrols around the village? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, they could walk out of the village if they didn't take the road. They would be able to go out of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They would be able to go out of the village?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, and then they were in the other part of the Kiseljak pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Muslim inhabitants of Rotilj ever went into Kiseljak, went into town to conduct business?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Sometimes some of them were given permission to visit a doctor or something in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on those occasions, they would actually pass out through the main checkpoint; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Croat inhabitants of Rotilj during this time?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you heard statements that persons were being kept in Rotilj for exchanges. Who told you that? Was that Josip Boro, the mayor?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, and Vinko Lucic, the liaison officer from HVO as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who made any such exchanges? Who organised any such exchanges?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: There was an exchange committee in Kiseljak, it consisted of several people, and they dealt with the exchanges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those exchanges of persons who asked to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Not only -- no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony is there were people who were forcibly exchanged who didn't want to be exchanged; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's also true because some of these people, they were exchanged to areas where they didn't want to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying they wanted to be exchanged but maybe not to Visoko and they went to Visoko, or they didn't want to be exchanged at all?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, in fact, it has nothing to do with exchange, it has to do with the fact that people were not safe there and they wanted to leave, so with or without exchange, they just wanted to leave the Kiseljak pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the people who were exchanged were people who wanted to leave the Kiseljak pocket; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said there were claims of forcible rape made to you from one or more residents of Rotilj. Do you know whether statements were taken from such persons or were they ever examined by a physician?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know of that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also related a conversation with Vinko Lucic in November of '93 when he said there was an investigation ongoing of some incident in Rotilj that had caused the death of, I believe, one person. Were you given the facts concerning that incident? What happened? Who were the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: He only told us that these were three or four men in uniform. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no other facts concerning whether they were drunk, whether they were from another area who had been displaced, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the ethnic mix of Kiseljak and Kresevo before the war and at some point during your tour, and there are dramatic reductions in the Muslim population of those two municipalities, according to these statistics. Can you tell the court, of the individuals who apparently left those municipalities, how many of them left before the conflict broke out in those municipalities in 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know when they left or died or whatever. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many of them left when the BH army pulled out or was defeated and retreated from those villages in the Kiseljak enclave in which there was a BH army presence?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Which villages are you referring to that BiH army would have retreated from?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, for example, in the village of Gomionica, when there was a battle that went on for some weeks between BH army units and the HVO. Do you know, did any of the civilian population pull out as the BH army withdrew from its positions, or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It was not during my stay in Bosnia so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that on or about the 25th of October, 1993, Emil Harah was replaced as the commander of the Bobovac brigade in Vares, a brigade depicted on Exhibit 431. Were you told who had ordered the removal of Emil Harah as brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I wasn't told. I was just told by Rajic that Harah was removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Several days after this event, were you informed that Rajic had been removed by order of Mate Boban? Did you gain that information in any form?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, please? Mr. President, Defence Exhibit 154 and the French translation 154A is a daily report of the ECMM, co-authored by this witness, and I would ask that it be placed before him.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D154 and D154A for the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, Major, is this a daily report co-authored by you and an ECMM colleague dated November 11, 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: You asked the question to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Major, you were asked a question. If you don't mind, when you answer, please look at the Judges. All right? Thank you. Yes, Mr. Hayman asked you a question, if you would be able to identify or to recognise this document. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes. It is an ECMM document, and my name is under it, but I wasn't there at the time. I was on leave. It is just a block in the computer, why my name's there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this report -- I apologise, Mr. President. My microphone goes off periodically, but I don't think it's a problem. I simply can turn it back on. In this report in paragraph 1(b) --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I can assure you that it's not the President that's having an effect on your microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this report, is there, in paragraph 1(b), can you add anything based on conversations with your ECMM colleagues or otherwise to the statement as follows. This is the fifth bullet point under paragraph 1(b): "The big rumour in the streets of Kiseljak is that Ivica Rajic, commander HVO Kiseljak, is not in command anymore, and for the time being replaced by General Petkovic. The Croatian Press stated that Rajic is sacked of his duties by order from the Office of the President of the Croatian Republic Herceg-Bosna, Mate Boban, due to heavy condition of defence of territory in Central Bosnia and co-relations with UNHCR and UNPROFOR and the course of investigations on responsibilities." Major, can you add anything to that report?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Only that it's not something I reported, that it is, as it says, a rumour in the streets, and something about the Press. So I cannot add anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you if you have anything to add to the passage at paragraph 7 of this same report on the next page, which is a comment. First, let me add, comments are the views of the author; is that what it means in ECMM format, to have a comment?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The comment reads as follows: "It is still not clear what is going on in the Kiseljak area, but the situation is tense. CANBAT advised everybody to be escorted when moving into Kiseljak (this is a little overdone). It seems that Rajic has been replaced because of his attitude towards UNHCR last week. This can cause another internal problem in Kiseljak since Rajic has a sort of a private army." Do you have anything to add to that statement, Major?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No. It's not my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with it or do you disagree with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, defence counsel is asking the witness, first of all, to comment on a statement that he didn't even make, and then he's asking him whether he agrees with it. He simply can't be asked to give evidence in this fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Objection sustained, especially since the witness said that he didn't write it and that his name is there only because of the computer. I think that the witness has already answered, Mr. Hayman. Please move to another question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described learning of threats made to, I believe, UNHCR by Ivica Rajic. Can you describe those threats in any more detail?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: We heard from Vinko Lucic, liaison officer, that Rajic had threatened a UNHCR officer; and from UNHCR, I don't remember which person from UNHCR, we heard that a field officer was threatened with his life by Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Ivica Rajic what you would term an aggressive individual?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, he didn't look really aggressive, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked whether you ever saw a report of investigation into Stupni Do. Is it correct that on the 22nd of November, 1993, you met that day, in the headquarters of the HVO in Kiseljak, an HVO security officer from Mostar named Ivan Bandic who told you that he was investigating the matter of Stupni Do and, in general, all the matters where HVO soldiers were involved with war crimes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand Mr. Bandic to be part of the security service apparently headquartered or based in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
