utterances.text: He just told us that he was from the headquarters and that he was a security officer. I don't know where he belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand him to report then to entities in Mostar not depicted on Exhibit 431?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: He didn't tell us whom he reported to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I offer into evidence Exhibits D153, D154, and D154A.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to both of those documents. First of all, D153 is a document which the witness stated that he didn't recognise. Secondly, D154 is a document which the witness stated was not authored by him; he cannot recognise any of the comments in the document. He simply can't authenticate any of these documents, so they should not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Then I'll proceed to ask the witness. I hadn't rested -- completed my questions, and I'd ask that the two exhibits be placed before the witness, D153 and D154.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Continue, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning your attention, Major, to Exhibit D153, the background report concerning Fojnica. First of all, on the last page of that report, do you recognise your initials?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, did you place your initials on that document on or about the 6th of -- excuse me, the 12th of June, 1996, when you tendered a copy of this report to a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take this report from your own personal archives and records pertaining to your service in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it an accurate and authentic copy of a report that was, in fact, generated by the ECMM at the time?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let me ask you to turn your attention to Exhibit D154. That is the two-page Monitor Team Daily Report dated November 11, 1993, and let me ask you: First of all, do you recognise the initials in the lower left-hand corner of the first page as those of Mr. Stutt who was, at the time, the chief of the regional centre Zenica for the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't recognise his initials. He was HCC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "HCC"?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: "Head of the Coordination Centre."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the -- first of all, do you know who Lars Jensen is?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Danish monitor in ECMM.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he serve on the V-3 team with you?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, he didn't. Maybe he went a couple of days with me, but he served together with Carstensen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when you were absent, apparently due to leave, was he assigned during that period of time to the V-3 team?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the court that this report is, in fact, an ECMM report? Can you tell the court that? Can you confirm that to the court?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer both exhibits, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Both documents are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I have concluded my examination. Thank you, Mr. President, and thank you, Major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that Mr. Cayley wants to exercise his right of redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I do. Thank you, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. Cayley:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked a number of questions in your cross-examination on matters that were not referred to in your examination-in-chief, and I'd like to develop that with you. You were asked specifically a question about access between the Kiseljak pocket and the Vitez pocket, and you mentioned that there were a number of mountain roads that could be taken between these two pockets. Can you tell the Judges about those mountain roads?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, there isn't much to tell about these roads. They were just mountain roads which we could use to go to an area of Kiseljak or Fojnica. It was partly through BiH territory. But sometimes we didn't see any soldiers. The roads were not closed; there were no checkpoints. There's nothing much to say about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that linked Vitez and Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were no large formations of Bosnian soldiers, no military fortifications on these roads?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, not on the roads, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked a number of questions about the road between Kiseljak and Visoko that was damaged around about the 9th of October of 1993. How big was that hole in the road?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Somewhere between 10 and 15 metres wide and, I think, 4 to 5 metres deep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a big hole, isn't it, in the ground?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, yeah. Well, just part of the road was gone and it slid into the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were informed that on or about the 12th of October of 1993, Colonel Blaskic ordered Mr. Rajic to fix the road.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, that was the -- Vinko Lucic told us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you actually used that road on the 20th of October of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the hole had been filled in?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that that road was repaired some time before the 20th of October of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when it was finished, but, of course, they had to start before the 20th, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a big job, isn't it, to do, between the 12th of October and the 20th of October of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It was a big hole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Faster than the repair of Dutch roadworks?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, they tend to take their time, but I cannot compare that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked a number of questions about the Muslims in the village of Rotilj, and I think you stated that the Muslims in Rotilj were not safe in any place, and then my learned friend Mr. Hayman added some commentary, and he said you weren't able to make a comparison. Now, can you state for the transcript what you mean by the fact that Muslims in Kiseljak were not safe anywhere?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, I mean that they weren't safe -- they didn't feel secure. They were afraid of harassment and injuries, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: People were really frightened in Rotilj village, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cayley. Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning, Major Meijboom.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just have a few clarifications. You mentioned that, when you visited the front-line, "I had heard Stanic announcing that all Muslims should be killed," and even nailed, as you said, even nailed to a cross and so on. Would this be a very personal view, or do you think he is reflecting the view of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It was his view which he stated every time when we met him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was it implemented, you think, the implementation followed his view?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: By his soldiers, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I didn't see anything of these results, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So you don't know. Then, in Rotilj, you had women who claimed to be raped.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was there any complaint of that and was it presented to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I know it was also under investigation of U.N. Civ. Po., United Nations Civil Police, but I don't know anything of the results of that investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But who was supposed to take the matter in hand? Was it the HVO or the United Nations police?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, in fact, it should have been done by the police in Kiseljak because it's a civil crime, I think, but it was done together with United Nations civil police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was there any result?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No punishment?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You don't know. And then concerning the attack on Stupni Do, you saw trucks, three trucks coming from Stupni Do with soldiers whom you heard complaining that they had a dirty job.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Could you describe more what you heard? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I don't know what they did. It's just what they told to the other team leader and he transferred it to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But they said it to the other team leader?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: They said that -- they didn't go into detail, they just said they had to do a job they didn't like and that they had nothing to do with what happened the day before or two days before in Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So it was vague. There was no indication of the kind of job they did.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, they weren't specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Weren't specific. They said that they didn't like it.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you hear that more often, that a few soldiers didn't like what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They liked it?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I don't know. They didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, concerning the removal of Rajic. Of course, this -- if you are in a position to tell me. Do you think removal of such an important officer in the army should come from the top, or can the commander remove his subordinates?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, the commander can remove his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But he was not removed -- was he removed by Colonel Blaskic or by Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You don't know that. But you heard that Rajic received orders directly from Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: He did not. And you mentioned -- I gather that he would sometimes be reluctant to execute the orders of Colonel Blaskic. He would not execute them immediately.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, if you refer to the repair of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: It happened, but it didn't happen immediately, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But he executed them --

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: -- all the same?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But otherwise, he would execute the orders. He did not --

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what kind of orders Mr. Rajic got from his commander, so I can't know which orders he followed or he didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The one concerning the road, you knew about it?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: That he took some time to execute it?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But he could not continue refusing?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So being in the area, could you say that the authority of Colonel Blaskic was not disputed?

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: No, I can't say it. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: He was the commander.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And he had the authority in hand.

utterances.speaker: OSCAR MEIJBOOM
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Shahabuddeen has no questions, nor do I. Major, the Tribunal thanks you for having come to testify at the request of the Prosecutor. Registrar, could we have the witness accompanied out of the courtroom, please? (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley -- I don't know whether Mr. Harmon or Mr. Cayley. How do you want to use this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We don't have any further witnesses to proceed with, Mr. President, but my learned friend, Mr. Harmon, has some evidence that he does wish to offer to the court at this point. It can probably be done before lunch. It's not going to take very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Right now, you mean? About how long do we need for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Five minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Five minutes. Well, I think the interpreters could grant us the five minutes. Very well. Thank you so much. Mr. Harmon, for the presentation of some additional evidence. At your own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, and counsel. Mr. President, we would tender an exhibit to the Trial Chamber, and I will explain what this exhibit is as soon as it is distributed. If I could have the assistance of the usher, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 432.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we tender this exhibit in respect of evidence that was led about the shelling in Zenica. As the Trial Chamber may recall, there was testimony from an investigating judge who investigated the events around the Zenica shelling. There were a number of photographs showing the effect of the Zenica shelling, including bodies of those victims who died as a result. The Trial Chamber asked us at one point during the course of the presentation of that evidence whether there was any proof connecting the shelling to the deaths of the individuals who were depicted in the photograph. We have secured from Dr. Faruk Turkic, who is a specialist in pathology and a previous witness who testified before Your Honours, a statement that reports on the connection between the bodies that were visible in the photographs and their cause of death. So this is to augment the testimony and the evidence in respect of the Zenica shelling, and we offer it accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. No comments from Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We have no objections other than those previously stated, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I understand the nuance that you're making. It is admitted subject to the previous comments. I think that Mr. Harmon merely wanted to show in this document that -- it is called -- this is the report further to the 13 people killed at the front of the Zenica store on the 13th of April. Very well. We're going to adjourn now until the 13th of July, Monday, 13th of July, at 2.30. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 12.55 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 13th day of July, 1998, at 2.30 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
